idiom.source: the fib adapter + self->spawn() from a behavior + examples/custom_type (CAF_ADD_TYPE_ID for std::vector<uint64_t>)
idiom.note: (vector) / (vector, position, sorts, results), the vector moved into the mail and out of a mutable-reference handler; children spawned into the work-stealing pool, the root's seeds before the window

caveats: CAF's scheduler is a work-stealing pool. 'cores' is a thread BUDGET; the workers are pinned one per CPU via caf::thread_hook so the CPU set matches qb's exactly, but CAF still steals across them and places every runnable actor dynamically, which qb's statically placed actors cannot do -- a scheduler that balances against one that does not is part of what this cell measures

wait=1 and wait=0 are the SAME configuration for CAF -- its shipped defaults (aggressive-poll-attempts=100, steal-interval=10); the sweep in docs/TUNING.md section 1 found every more aggressive profile slower and no profile was invented for this benchmark

in the work-stealing pool an actor made ready by a message sent from a worker is prepended to THAT worker's queue (worker::delay), so sender and receiver stay on one thread until the other worker steals; how many hops cross a core is the scheduler's decision, not the adapter's, and is not reported
no caf-detached row for this benchmark: one private thread per actor at this actor count would measure the OS scheduler, not CAF (frameworks/caf-detached/README.md)
CAF 1.1.0 builds itself at C++17 -- its own CMake sets the standard -- while qb and the harness are C++20. Forcing CAF to C++20 was not done: it would measure a build CAF does not ship

a child spawned from a worker is enqueued on THAT worker and stolen from there, so with cores=2 the tree is balanced dynamically; qb's cell keeps each half of the first split on its seed's core because qb has no cross-core spawn -- see benchmarks/savina/quicksort.md
